rationale: The candidate space is deliberately small and contains one mandatory behavior family plus two optional timing features.
Accuracy, rule-error rate, commission errors and omissions are not entered as separate equally weighted features because they partially encode the same response events.
External clinical outcomes and treatment-group differences are forbidden inputs to feature-set selection.

Recovery-score normalization uses a stable target-rule/mapping-matched reference for B, S and V because A↔B switching changes both response mapping and GO-stimulus identity; the immediate pre-switch reference is an eligibility/readiness check, not the q reference.

balanced_rule_success.definition: 0.5 * (Jeffreys-smoothed GO hit probability + Jeffreys-smoothed NO-GO correct-rejection probability)
notes: Equal weighting of GO and NO-GO conditional success prevents target/non-target frequency from changing the meaning of the feature.
Jeffreys smoothing prevents perfect or zero observed proportions from producing degenerate probability estimates.
B_ref is calculated from the stable target-rule recovery reference collected in RULE_CALIBRATION, not from the immediate pre-switch current-rule reference.
The comparison scale combines uncertainty in target-rule reference probabilities with expected sampling variance of the current window under those reference probabilities.
The denominator does not use the observed postchallenge success rate, so poor performance cannot reduce its own standardized deficit by inflating its variance.
Only correct GO trials enter the latency feature.
The RT reference comes from the same target-rule recovery reference used for B and must match the post-switch rule and GO-stimulus identity.
Faster correct responses are not penalized; impulsive fast errors are captured by balanced_rule_success.
Timing reference scale is max(1.4826*MAD_target_rule_ref, qualified device timing floor).
Robust scale is 1.4826*MAD of correct GO reaction times.
The timing reference is drawn from the same target-rule recovery reference used for B; immediate pre-switch RT is not used as the q baseline.
The timing floor prevents near-zero baseline MAD from creating arbitrarily large ratios.

score_definition.component_scores: z_j = -d_j, where d_j >= 0 is the prespecified feature deficit
score_definition.composite: q_e(t) = sum_j w_j * z_j(t); weights sum to 1

interpretation.zero: no detected deficit relative to the stable target-rule recovery reference under the selected feature definition
interpretation.negative: one or more included feature deficits remain
interpretation.recovery_rule: q_e(t) >= -delta for the full stability window

score_definition.rationale: Above-reference performance in one feature cannot cancel a clinically or behaviorally relevant deficit in another feature.

decision_rule: Reject any candidate that fails a hard gate.
Evaluate the leave-one-trial robustness gate across the full prespecified delta x stability grid; do not choose the threshold combination that makes a model pass.
If model B passes all hard gates, retain B unless a more complex model is required by a prespecified measurement failure that B does not resolve.
If B fails and multiple enriched models pass, prefer the lowest complexity rank.
Within the same complexity rank, prefer lower feature missingness and lower leave-one-trial instability.
Do not prefer a model merely because it reduces censoring or produces shorter recovery latency.
Document all candidate results, including rejected definitions, before freezing the Phase 1 model.

robustness_grid.rule: Apply leave-one-trial perturbation across every prespecified delta x stability combination and use the worst terminal-state flip fraction for the hard gate.
